Vulnerability.Name: Unrestricted File Upload in Certificate Module
Vulnerability.Description: The trainee certificate upload endpoint /api/cert/upload accepts arbitrary file types including .php, .jsp, and .aspx. An attacker can upload a web shell and execute commands as the application user. No content-type or magic-byte validation is performed.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Whitelist allowed extensions to .pdf, .png, .jpg only. Validate file magic bytes server-side. Store uploads outside the web root.

Vulnerability.Name: Hard-Coded API Key in Mobile Build
Vulnerability.Description: The Android trainee app ships with a hard-coded API key for the certification backend. The key has full read/write privileges and can be extracted by any attacker who decompiles the APK.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Rotate the leaked key immediately. Implement per-user OAuth tokens. Store secrets in the Android Keystore, not in source.

Vulnerability.Name: Server-Side Request Forgery in Avatar Importer
Vulnerability.Description: The /api/profile/avatar?url= endpoint fetches arbitrary URLs server-side without validation. Attacker can pivot to internal services including the AWS metadata endpoint at 169.254.169.254 and exfiltrate IAM credentials.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Block private IP ranges and link-local addresses. Use an HTTP proxy with an allowlist. Disable IMDSv1 on EC2 instances.

Vulnerability.Name: Verbose Error Messages Disclose Stack Traces
Vulnerability.Description: Production error pages expose full Java stack traces including library versions, file paths, and database driver details. Useful for attacker reconnaissance to identify exploitable framework versions.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Set spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=false and configure a generic error page. Log details server-side only.

Vulnerability.Name: Weak JWT Signing Algorithm Accepted
Vulnerability.Description: The session token validator accepts JWTs signed with the "none" algorithm. Any attacker who obtains a valid token structure can forge tokens for any user including administrators.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Hard-code the expected algorithm to RS256 in jwt.verify() options. Reject any token whose header alg field is "none".

Vulnerability.Name: Database Backups Stored Without Encryption
Vulnerability.Description: Nightly database dumps are written to /var/backups/db as plain SQL. Files are world-readable and contain trainee PII including passport numbers, dates of birth, and seafarer's identification document numbers.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Encrypt backups with GPG using a dedicated key. Restrict /var/backups/db to root only. Rotate dumps to encrypted offsite storage.

Vulnerability.Name: Exposed phpMyAdmin Interface
Vulnerability.Description: phpMyAdmin is reachable at https://db-primary.nykfil.local/pma without IP restriction. Default admin credentials (admin/admin) still functional. Direct database access from any internet-facing host.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Remove phpMyAdmin from the public web root. If needed, bind to localhost only and tunnel via SSH. Force password reset on all DB accounts.

Vulnerability.Name: Slow Query Log Contains Plaintext Passwords
Vulnerability.Description: The MySQL slow query log captures the full text of UPDATE statements that include password hashes and reset tokens. Log file is rotated to /backup with the same world-readable permissions as the database backups.
Vulnerability.Remediation: Disable slow query log in production, or sanitize logged SQL. Move log rotation to an encrypted destination with restricted ACL.
